steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Beat sugar and butter together in a large mixing bowl until light and fluffy. Beat in eggs and milk. Add flour, cornmeal, lemon juice, and lemon zest. Mix until smooth. Pour mixture into prepared pastry crust.
Bake pie in the preheated oven until center is set, about 40 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Bill Clinton's Lemon Chess Pie
raw_recipe.description: This lemon chess pie has a rich and smooth filling made with milk and eggs, flavored with lemon juice and lots of zest for a sweet and tangy dessert.
raw_recipe.name: Bill Clinton's Lemon Chess Pie

Bake pie in the preheated oven until center is set, about 40 minutes.

review.reviewBody: I thought that the recipe was really a great one. The only thing is...if you are using a regular (not deep dish) pie crust, this recipe makes two pies. I found this out the hard way. I thought that since it says it only makes one pie that I would double the recipe for two...Right?? Wrong...I ended up with four pies. This is not a bad thing, though. The neighborhood just loved it too!!

Delicious! Thanks for sharing! I did use 1 1/2 cup sugar and I don’t do dairy so used 1/2 cup unsweetened soy milk and it was delicious! I used a glass pie dish and it took about 45 min to cook. Covered the edges in foil last 5 min.
Cut the sugar! VERY SWEE! So the second time I made it, I cut the sugar by 1/2 a cup, and it’s much better. I also had some fresh blueberries, so I dotted them into the pie, and it was incredible!

This is close but NOT the original recipe & in my opinion, you messed it up. Anyway, here is what's different the total liquid is correct, but the distribution is not his & is also not improved. Use 1/2 cup fresh squeezed lemon juice and 3/4 cup milk. I reduce the sugar to 1 1/2 cup (a bit sweet with 2 whole cups). To those saying it's runny, you didn't cook it long enough. If it's still giggly, it's not done, stick a knife in it -- when it comes out clean, it's done & not before! Every oven is a little different. Also make sure you don't forget the flour and cornmeal - it makes a difference. I put fresh blueberries in the last one & it was phenominal!

Really enjoyed this, with a few adaptations. Definitely sweet enough with 1-1/2 cups sugar instead of 2. I doubled the amount of lemon juice and added an extra tablespoon of zest. Also added a few splashes of vanilla extract. Next time we might substitute cream for the milk.
One recipe was plenty to fill a deep dish pie shell, although it did take longer to heat. 40 minutes was not enough (we used a toaster/convection oven). I kept an eye on it and ended up cooking about 55 minutes. Top was nicely browned but not burnt. Filling was still soupy but pie set nicely after resting on the counter for a while. We tried the first piece while still slightly warm. Delicious & perfectly tart. Pie did weep a bit, but not a problem (and I bet it won't do again once refrigerated).
I hope it's not apocryphal that this is one of Bill Clinton's favorites. We made it to console ourselves after the debacle of the 2016 election.

Have never made a home made lemon chess pie until tonight. Followed the recipe pretty closely because of the reviews.
Reduced the sugar by 1/3 c. but think 1/2 c. reduction would bring out the lemon flavor more. Also, had a deep dish pie crust that I did not thaw and it cooked perfectly including the edges. There is to much liquid so next time I'll reduce the quantity of milk by half (I used fat free half and half because it's what I had.) Also, even though the photo shows a more custard type layer at the top I didn't expect that and was looking for a more smooth consistency throughout. Going to refrigerate and let it firm up some. This needs to bake the day before you need it. The flavor was nice lemony but very sweet.

I made this pie today on Election Day & it was easy & turned out perfect. I used a roll out Pillsbury crust in a 9 inch pie plate & cooked at 350 for 45 minutes,and it was very delicious. I used only one cup sugar (by accident but it tasted great!)& 1/2 cup of lemon (because we like it tart),real butter,& fat free milk. Great easy recipe! Thanks for sharing! (and we LOVE Bill Clinton!!) ; )

I've made this twice in the past week. My husband and I both prefer it to lemon meringue pie. I've made pies professionally for quite a few years. This recipe makes a 10 inch pie. There is too much filling for a 9 inch pie. I used 1/2 heavy cream the first time and it was almost too rich and interfered with the tart/sweet lemon flavor. The second time I used 1/2 milk and 1/2 half and half. That is the combination we prefer. I only had 2 lemons, which made about 2 tablespoons of zest and it was plenty. You need to use butter, no substitutes. This pie is meant to be rich and sweet, combined with the unique texture from the cornmeal. Wonderful. Will be my go to lemon pie from now on. I did have to increase the baking time for a bit, but just kept an eye on it. This pie benefits from sitting for a few hours and we like it best cold.

I made this pie today and it was absolutely wonderful. My husband and I agree that it's a "keeper". Based on others' comments, I was concerned with having filling left over so I used a store-bought piecrust (Pillsbury) (found in the dairy case in the long skinny box) and rolled it out bigger so that it would fit in my 10" pyrex pie plate. It ended up being perfect as I had just the right amount of filling. I also used half and half instead of the milk and the next time I will cut the sugar down to 1 1/2 cups. I cooked it for 50 minutes which I think was perfect for the 10" pie and it set up very nicely in the fridge - it cut beautifully!!

Very good, very easy. I made it with Meyer lemons, so I took the suggestions of some posters by increasing the juice and cutting back the sugar to 1 1/2 cups. It was lemon-y but very mild. I made it the night before I needed it and left it in the refrigerator overnight, and the texture was just right.

Yep, made it several times and used buttermilk in lieu of the milk or 1/2 buttermilk and 1/2 half'n'half. Pretty creamy stuff. Used 1/2 teaspoon intense natural lemon extract with the zest. All these little changes are fine. Only commnent otherwise is the oven setting may be too high and the time too short. I moved it back to 300F and let it cook 20 min longer and it really set up. At 350F and 40minutes it didn't set up in the center. Also when you lower an oven setting and increase the cook time, more H2O evaporates and that contributes to the custard to set easily. But not an issue really.

Alterations: 1.5C sugar, .5C lemon juice, .75C milk. 1 hr in the oven, could have used even another 5-10 minutes more. Used homemade pie crust and glass baking dish. Isaac liked it a lot. I thought it was fine, not great.
Simple recipe that’s easy to make. I used six lemons to zest and squeeze for juice. I made a ten-inch pie. Multiply each ingredient amount by 1.24 to convert from a nine in to a ten inch pie pan.

We have made this recipe five or six times. Always delicious. Not sure how it worked the first time but it made one very full pie that took an hour and a half to bake. Since then we have either cut down the ingredients a tad or made two thinner pies. Never disappoints.
Well somebody shut my mouth before I eat this whole pie! A delicious delight.

I've been making this pie for years it is truly delicious I do reduce the sugar a lil and throw in a lil extra cornmeal cause I like it. I normally just use lemon juice in a bottle cause its what I have on hand but im doing the whole zest and fresh squeezed lemons tonight just to see what the difference is.
I didn’t make any changes. Excellent pie, very tangy!
This recipe is very friendly and delicious
I baked my for 40 min and it seems to be hard not custard like. Oven was set at 350 maybe next time less time.
I am now the official Lemon Chess pie maker in the family! Once I saw who's recipe it was, I just knew it would be good!
